Subject: RFP: Identity & Access Controls — Lockstone Health

Diego,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Lockstone is completing an enterprise review of vendor identity controls as part of our procurement cycle. We have a focused section on privileged access, self-service onboarding, SCIM provisioning, SSO (SAML/OIDC), and role-based admin controls.

Attached is the Lockstone IAM questionnaire PDF (short form). Our procurement timeline is tight — we need your completed answers and supporting evidence by 2026-11-04. Specific asks:
- Confirm support for automated SCIM provisioning (user/group sync), SCIM delta handling, and provisioning error reporting.
- Describe RBAC primitives, custom roles, and admin separation controls.
- Provide documentation or sample configs for SAML SSO and OIDC (SP-initiated + IdP metadata).
- Explain privileged access escalation review workflows (time-bounded elevation, approval audit trail).
- Provide SOC2/Security evidence links or attachments.

Point of contact for tech clarifications: me (Maya Chen). Procurement contact: it_procurement@lockstonehealth.com.

Thanks — looking forward.

Maya Chen
Senior IT Procurement
Lockstone Health

Subject: Re: RFP: Identity & Access Controls — Lockstone Health

Maya — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear timeline. We can meet your 2026-11-04 window.

High-level commitments up front:
- SCIM: Full SCIM 2.0 provisioning supported (create/update/delete for users + groups), delta syncs, bulk operations, and a configurable retry/error webhooks surface.
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated) and OIDC (authorization code + PKCE for clients). We provide metadata and example integrations for major IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Ping).
- RBAC & Admin Controls: Role model supports admin roles, delegated admin scopes, and least-privilege custom roles. Changes to admin roles are auditable and require owner approval for elevated scopes in managed accounts.
- Privileged access: Time-limited elevation via approval flow or Just-In-Time (JIT) token issuance; audit trail retained per retention policy; optional periodic recertification workflows.

I'm attaching a short consolidated response and sample SCIM payload. Marissa (security solutions) and Neha (sales engineering) are on copy for technical deep-dive and evidence pack. If you can confirm the preferred evidence delivery method (Drive or secure upload), we'll push the items there and call out any gaps.

Next steps requested from Lockstone: confirm the IdP(s) you intend to use and whether you require SCIM provisioning to be one-way or two-way.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Diego / Maya — 

Following up with the more detailed technical answers you requested; I've pasted concise responses inline against each Lockstone question and attached configuration samples.

----- Original message from Lockstone IAM questionnaire -----
> Q: Does Redwood support automated user and group provisioning via SCIM? How do you handle deltas and conflicts?

A: Yes. Redwood implements SCIM 2.0 endpoints for Users and Groups. Delta handling: we support incremental sync using lastModified filtering and etag-based concurrency to avoid overwrite conflicts. In the event of attribute collisions we return standard SCIM error codes and expose an audit+retry endpoint. Administrators can configure mapping rules in the console (attribute mappings, transform hooks). Logs include per-attempt status, error payload, and resolution guidance. See attached redwood-scim-sync-sample.json for example payload and mapping snippet.

> Q: Describe RBAC model and ability to create custom admin roles. Can you separate "billing/admin" from "model-serving/admin"?

A: Yes. RBAC is role-based with resource scoping. Built-in roles cover Billing Admin, Account Admin, Deployment Admin, and Viewer. Customers can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions (action-level) and scoped to projects/environments. Role assignment changes are tracked; role-to-user history is queryable via the audit API. You can and should separate billing functions from serving/ops functions by assigning distinct roles.

> Q: Privileged elevation & approval flow — time limits, approvers, and retention?

A: The platform supports JIT elevation that issues time-limited privileged tokens once an approval workflow is completed. Approval chains can include multi-step approvers and an optional expiration (default 1 hour, configurable). All approvals and sessions are recorded; we retain logs for 90 days by default and longer with enterprise add-on. Evidence in the attached playbook details the approval lifecycle and sample audit logs.

> Q: SAML/OIDC configuration examples and metadata?

A: Attached: redwood-sso-saml-config-guide.pdf with SAML metadata, SP-entity ID, ACS URL, and example claims mapping. For OIDC we provide client registration examples and recommended scopes. We support enforcing conditional access via IdP claims and can require mfa: true for admin roles.

> Q: Evidence (SOC2, test accounts, penetration test summaries) — what can you share?

A: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and provide redacted pen test summaries. For RFP timelines we can upload SOC2 stub and pen-test digest to a secure drive link. Full reports require a signed attestation.

----- end quoted block -----

Marissa
Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sso-saml-config-guide.pdf, redwood-privileged-access-playbook-20261102.pdf, redwood-scim-sync-sample.json
